text.p: Prime Hospitality Corp said Wednesday it had retained Montgomery Securities as its financial advisor to evaluate and enter into a sale/leaseback transaction with some of its hotels.
It said in a statement it would use the proceeds of the deal to accelerate the growth of its proprietary hotel brands.

Prime owns or manages 112 hotels under its proprietary trade names AmeriSuites and Wellesley Inns as well as under franchise agreements with national hotel chains including Marriott, Radisson and Sheraton, among others.
It said it had selected nine full-service hotels for the transaction.
"The hotels are located in the Northeast, Mountain and Pacific regions of the United States and are operated primarily under franchise agreements with Sheraton, Crowne Plaza and Ramada," it said.
For the twelve months ended June 30, 1997, the hotels generated revenues and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $54.6 million and $19.6 million, respectively, it said.

Prime said it expected to complete the deal transaction by the end of 1997, adding that it will likely pursue a second transaction in 1998 involving the sale/leaseback of certain of its remaining full-service hotels.
